_doc.purpose: Reference profiles shipped with lilkuzco_kinetics v0.1.0. Consumers may load these directly or use them as worked examples.
_doc.units: SI throughout. Mass kg, thrust N, area m^2, Isp s (REAL values - the sim applies propulsion.exhaust_velocity_scale), pressure Pa, altitude m above the sea-level datum.
_doc.note: Specific impulse is declared as its real-world figure so engines stay recognisable. See SCALE-AUDIT.md for what the sim does with it.

profiles._note: Unguided ballistic reference. Streamlined, no lifting surface, no seeker - the simplest thing the library can fly, and the case the ballistic solver is checked against.

Light, draggy, deliberately low ballistic coefficient. Exists for the RB3 golden test: dropped from the Karman line it ACCELERATES in thin air, then DECELERATES as the air thickens - the counterintuitive result that only falls out if the atmosphere model is right.

Short-range PN interceptor. Hard 1.2 s boost then a guided coast, which is what real point-defence missiles do - all the energy up front, spend it manoeuvring. Fins give it turn authority after burnout; at 400 m/s it can pull 37 g and at 100 m/s only 2.3 g, which is invariant I6 doing its job.

The same airframe with a budget head: plain PN only (CHEAP gates out augmented PN per RC2), a narrow 20-degree gimbal, and poor counter-countermeasures. Included so the difference a good seeker makes is visible rather than asserted.

Long-range, lofted. A bigger motor and a 1200 m seeker mean it burns out with the target still far away, so it genuinely flies the whole state machine: BOOST under the loft bias, a long unpowered MIDCOURSE on PN, then TERMINAL. The short-range interceptor above never sees MIDCOURSE because it arrives before burnout.

Winged, unpowered, high aspect ratio. Exists for the two lift tests: that C_L peaks near 15 degrees and then collapses (RB4), and that a sustained maximum-C_L turn bleeds speed because induced drag has to be paid for (RB4b/I3).

The reference launch vehicle: 19,627 kg on the pad to put 100 kg in orbit. Two kerolox stages giving 2400 m/s of ideal delta-v against a 2230 m/s budget - a 7.6% margin, which is not padding. A first stage burning through thick air runs at sea-level Isp for much of its burn and delivers about 13 m/s less than the vacuum equation promises, so a design sized exactly to the budget arrives short. Sea-level T/W is 1.80. Structural fraction is 12% per stage, which is also what caps the design: stage 1 cannot exceed a mass ratio of about 8 no matter how much propellant it carries, which is precisely why the second stage exists.

Lifts off cleanly at T/W 1.50 and still fails, because delta-v and thrust are different problems. 1361 m/s of ideal delta-v against a 2230 m/s budget: 869 m/s short. It reaches the Karman line and falls back, which is the honest failure RD3 asks for.

The other failure mode, and the one that catches paper designs. Sea-level T/W is 0.95, so it never leaves the pad - but VACUUM T/W is 1.04, so judged on the vacuum thrust figure this vehicle looks flyable. It is not. That 9.9% gap between sea-level and vacuum thrust is exactly why RD5 specifies the sea-level number for the liftoff gate, and this profile exists to sit inside the gap.

Blunt body, drogue then main, sized from the entry it actually has to survive. C_d 1.35 over 14 m^2 on 500 kg is a ballistic coefficient of 26 kg/m^2 - a 4.2 m heat shield on a half-tonne capsule, which looks absurd next to a real one until you notice this atmosphere carries 1/155th of Earth's column mass. A capsule with a real-world beta of 400 arrives at the ground still supersonic. The shield has to be this big; the physics says so, and the shield is a visible component because of it. Chutes are staged: the drogue takes 18 kPa, the main only 5 kPa, so the main physically cannot open until the drogue has done its work.

The control for the blunt-body test (RE7): identical mass, sharply lower drag and a fine nose. It keeps its speed until it is deep in thick air, and because heating goes as v^3 it cooks. Its peak heating rate must come out ABOVE the blunt capsule's despite the smaller nose - that ordering is the whole insight.
A single main chute with no drogue, for the over-q shred test. Opening a 5 kPa canopy while still fast destroys it - which is the point of the deploy gate, and why the staged capsule above exists.
A registry payload. It has an airframe only so that a deorbit handoff has something to fly; in orbit its physics is the elements, not this.
